values.fieldLabel: Resume / CV (Please upload your CV as a PDF or Docx)

nodes.name: CV Submission Form
nodes.notes:
This form is the single entry point for the workflow.
Key decisions:
• Required fields enforce minimum viable candidate data (name + email).
• File input is restricted to PDF and DOCX to reduce OCR errors downstream.
• Additional validation is handled server-side to avoid relying solely on frontend controls.

nodes.name: CV Validation
nodes.notes:
This node performs server-side validation and normalization before any storage or AI processing.
Key decisions:
• MIME-type validation prevents renamed or unsupported files from entering the system.
• File size is capped (5MB) to protect OCR performance and API limits.
• Candidate name is normalized and sanitized to produce deterministic, filesystem-safe storage paths.
• Validation errors intentionally stop the workflow early to avoid wasted compute.

nodes.name: Supabase CV storage Bucket
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Persist uploaded CVs for traceability and reprocessing.

Key decisions:
• CVs are stored before AI matching to ensure no data loss if downstream steps fail.
• Date-based folders + normalized filenames enable easy auditing and retrieval.
• Supabase was chosen for its simple API, free tier, and compatibility with binary uploads.

parameters.text:
=You are an AI matching agent operating inside a workflow with external tools enabled.

You are given three distinct inputs, and you must treat them exactly as described.

Inputs
1. Candidate Metadata (JSON)

This JSON contains only metadata, not CV content. It includes:

First name: {{ $('CV Validation').item.json['First Name'] }}

Surname: {{ $('CV Validation').item.json.Surname }}

Email: {{ $('CV Validation').item.json.Email }}

Storage path: {{ $('CV Validation').item.json.storage_path }}

⚠️ This JSON does not contain skills, experience, education, or role history.
You must not infer or assume any professional details from this JSON.

2. CV File (Binary / Extracted Text)

Input: {{ $json.extractedText }}

Source: Uploaded CV file (PDF or DOCX)

You must:

Read and rely only on this extracted CV text to determine skills, experience, and qualifications.

If required information is not present in the CV text, treat it as missing. Do not guess.

3. Open Roles (Airtable Tool)

You have access to an Airtable tool that returns open roles only.
Each role includes:

Role Name

Department

Required Skills (array of strings)

Minimum Experience (years)

Location

Job Description

Seniority Level

You must retrieve role data exclusively via the Airtable tool.
Do not invent roles or reuse cached knowledge.

Mandatory Rules (No Exceptions)

You must use tools to read:

CV content (from extracted text)

Open roles (from Airtable)

If a tool has not returned data, you must not proceed as if it has.

If information is missing, return a result that reflects missing data instead of guessing.

Do not hallucinate skills, experience, or roles.

Do not assume seniority, years of experience, or role fit unless explicitly stated in the CV text.

Task

1. Extract skills and years of experience from the CV text.

2. For each Airtable role, compute a match score:

Skill match % =
(number of matching skills ÷ total required skills) × 100

If candidate experience is below the role’s minimum, reduce the score proportionally.

3. Select only the single highest-scoring role.

4. Determine match status:

    matched → at least one role evaluated and a best match selected

    no_match → roles exist but none meet a reasonable match threshold or airtable returned zero roles

5. Do not return secondary matches or explanations.

Output (Strict)

Return only valid JSON in the exact structure below.
No commentary, no markdown, no extra keys.

{
  "candidate": {
    "full_name": "string",
    "email": "string"
  },
  "match": {
    "role": "string or null",
    "match_score": "number or null",
    "status": "matched | no_match"
  }
}

nodes.name: AI Agent
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Analyze CV text against open roles and return a single best match.

Key decisions:
• Candidate metadata is treated as non-professional context and explicitly excluded from skill inference.
• Open roles must be retrieved via the Airtable tool to prevent hallucinated positions.
• The agent is instructed to return strict JSON only to ensure deterministic downstream logic.
• Missing information is handled explicitly rather than inferred, prioritizing accuracy over optimism.

nodes.name: Open Roles DB
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Serve as the single source of truth for open positions.

Key decisions:
• Roles are stored in a structured schema (skills, experience, seniority) to support AI evaluation.
• Access is restricted to a tool call so the AI cannot invent or reuse cached role data.
• This design allows roles to be updated independently without modifying the workflow.

nodes.name: SO Parser
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Enforce a strict JSON contract on AI responses.

Key decisions:
• Ensures downstream nodes receive predictable, typed data.
• Prevents free-text responses from breaking conditional logic.
• Acts as a safety layer between probabilistic AI output and deterministic automation.

nodes.name: OCR/CV parsing
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Convert uploaded CV files into plain text for AI analysis.

Key decisions:
• OCR/parsing is isolated from matching logic to keep responsibilities clear.
• Only extracted CV text is passed forward — no assumptions are made from metadata.
• Using Mistral avoids reliance on OpenAI while staying within free-tier constraints.

nodes.name: Candidate matched?
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Apply business rules to AI-generated match results.

Key decisions:
• A minimum match score threshold (≥75%) is enforced at the workflow level rather than inside the AI.
• This keeps business policy separate from AI reasoning and allows easy adjustment without prompt changes.
• Both status and score must pass to qualify a candidate as “matched.”

parameters.subject: Update on Your Application
parameters.message:
=Hi {{ $('CV Validation').item.json['First Name'] }},  

Thank you for taking the time to apply and for sharing your CV with us.  

At the moment, we don’t have any open roles that align with your background. This isn’t a reflection of your experience or qualifications, just the current availability on our side.  

We’ll keep your details on file and reach out if a suitable opportunity opens up. We appreciate your interest and wish you all the best in your ongoing search.  

Warm regards, 
Recruitment at company XYZ

nodes.name: Send 'No current opening' message
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Provide timely and respectful feedback to unmatched applicants.

Key decisions:
• Messaging is polite and non-rejecting to preserve employer brand.
• Sent automatically to ensure no candidate is left without a response.
• This path covers both low match scores and lack of suitable open roles.

nodes.name: Save matched candidate info to supabase table
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Persist matched candidate data for tracking and review.

Key decisions:
• Only candidates who pass the matching criteria are stored.
• Stored data includes references to the original CV file for future audits.
• This table can later support analytics, reporting, or manual review workflows.

nodes.name: Send details to HR
nodes.notes:
Purpose: Notify HR immediately when a strong candidate match is found.

Key decisions:
• Slack is used for fast, asynchronous internal communication.
• Only essential information is included to avoid exposing unnecessary personal data.
• Human review is intentionally kept in the loop before any hiring action.

parameters.content:
Server-side validation in this node is mandatory because frontend validation can be bypassed (malicious requests, API calls, or misconfigured clients).

This second validation layer protects downstream systems (storage, OCR, AI) from invalid, oversized, or disguised files and ensures the workflow fails fast and safely.

main.node: Save matched candidate info to supabase table
